author: Andrew Fisher
scope: Independent source review and isolated VM regression of shared flow safeguards

checks.name: Departure captures native Sub-hired fold state once
Discarded pane restores open and closed duplicate-key folds independently
One supplier never inherits another supplier's fold state
A different viewing date never inherits the previous date's fold state
Tab navigation never invokes full persistence capture or restore
An unchanged visible view accepts its pending reveal
A later user action cancels an older pending reveal
A hidden pane refuses its pending reveal
Leaving a tab cancels its pending reveal
Changing the Inventory drill cancels the earlier drill reveal
Registry refresh captures, calls native redraw and restores exactly once

findings: Departure capture precedes native hidden-pane disposal.
Arrival replays disclosure booleans before native tab scrolling; it does not restore old fields, focus or scroll.
Supplier, date, finance and trade context separate cached views.
Registry redraw retains the original refresh function and adds synchronous main-pane preservation.
Inventory mutation handlers remain native; delayed reveals check current view and user intent.

limitations: Uses synthetic DOM/state fixtures. Does not replace native browser, rendering, focus, scroll or service verification.
